Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that managed care can make it easier for low-income individuals to identify a usual source of care. According to one match, "Having a usual physician can be an effective tool in improving access to care for low-income populations, although it is most effective when combined with insurance coverage."

Another match suggests that managed care may help individuals from lower socioeconomic backgrounds navigate the healthcare system more effectively by providing them with access to primary care providers who are closer to their living areas. This can make it easier for them to find a usual source of care.

However, it's also mentioned in another match that the effectiveness of managed care in linking more low-income persons to a medical home is uncertain, and may have unintended consequences for uninsured persons. This implies that while managed care can be helpful, its impact on all individuals, particularly those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds, cannot be fully evaluated without further research.

In summary, based on these matches, it seems that managed care can be an effective tool in enabling low-income individuals to identify a usual source of care by providing them with access to primary care providers and other healthcare services.
